subject.title: Feature Request: Add parseMode config for Telegram channels

question: Should the Telegram plugin add a public channel/account parse or text-mode config, and which supported values/defaults should apply across sends, captions, edits, and streaming previews?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding this setting expands public config surface and changes Telegram escaping, rich-message compatibility, and security posture.

options.title: Add narrow plain/HTML config
options.body: Preserve current HTML-compatible delivery as the default and add an explicit plain/no-parse mode with account inheritance and full outbound-funnel coverage.

options.title: Design broader formatting modes
options.body: Include MarkdownV2, raw HTML, or entity-based modes only after maintainers settle escaping, custom emoji, and trust-boundary semantics.

options.title: Keep existing knobs only
options.body: Decline parse-mode config for now and continue improving targeted formatter behavior through `richMessages`, `markdown.tables`, and narrower rendering fixes.

recommendation.title: Add narrow plain/HTML config
recommendation.body: Preserve current HTML-compatible delivery as the default and add an explicit plain/no-parse mode with account inheritance and full outbound-funnel coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest routing signal from the prior review of this exact issue and follow-up work on the current Telegram formatting boundary.
